overview.project_context: The Clockwork Vault is a solo adventure set inside a sealed ancient machine complex. Guided by Custodian Vex, the player restores four connected systems—Resonance Engine, Broken Gallery, Warden Halls, and the Great Orrery—so the century-sealed gateway can reopen. The journey focuses on learning invented rules, recovering from readable setbacks, and seeing the vault visibly return to life.

journey.title: The Antechamber
journey.description: Meet Custodian Vex, learn why the vault is sealed, obtain the Custodian Key, and open the first objective chamber.

journey.title: The Resonance Engine
journey.description: Search scattered books to discover the hidden Left and Right target colors and which pillar must pulse, then experiment with the three pillar controls until the Engine matches the final state.

journey.title: The Broken Gallery
journey.description: Cross three route-selection levels by searching checkpoint barrels, repairing only marked gaps, managing limited blocks/ladders, and surviving the final Gremlin time challenge.

journey.title: The Warden Halls
journey.description: Cross three trap checkpoints using the Echo Pebble against wall-laser systems while avoiding floor traps and timing swinging ceiling axes.

journey.title: The Gremlin’s Workshop
journey.description: Route continuous power from the Generator through Ring 1, Ring 2, and Ring 3, repairing the network each time the Gremlin disrupts an earlier connection.

journey.title: The Vault Awakens
journey.description: Awaken the Great Orrery, reopen the century-sealed gateway, complete the story, and return safely.

gameplay_flow.title: The Journey Begins
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The player discovers the Clockwork Vault beneath forgotten ruins and crosses its entrance before understanding that the gateway opens only once every hundred years.

beats.title: From Forgotten Ruins to the Sealed Vault
beats.description: The player discovers the Clockwork Vault beneath forgotten ruins and crosses its ancient entrance. The gate immediately seals behind them, trapping the player inside a place caught in a century-long restoration cycle. In the Antechamber, Custodian Vex awakens and explains that the vault was not built to hide treasure; it was built to protect the Great Orrery. The machine has been dormant for centuries, and the entrance cannot reopen until its connected mechanisms are restored in sequence.

beats.title: The Custodian’s Warning
beats.description: Custodian Vex explains that previous visitors attempted the same journey but never restored the full system. Every chamber controls a necessary part of the vault: power distribution, access through the collapsed inner gallery, the ancient security halls, and the final network feeding the Great Orrery. The player must proceed because no other exit exists.

beats.title: Beginning the Restoration
beats.description: The journey proceeds through four gameplay objectives—Resonance Engine, Broken Gallery, Warden Halls, and Gremlin’s Workshop—before the restored Orrery opens the ending sequence.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: Vex directs the player to the central pedestal. Taking the Custodian Key activates the first seal and reveals the entrance to the Resonance Engine. From this point forward, every completed objective visibly awakens another section of the vault.
gameplay_flow.eyebrow: From Forgotten Ruins to the Sealed Vault

gameplay_flow.title: The Antechamber
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The Antechamber is a protected lobby and narrative introduction where the player first meets Custodian Vex.

beats.title: Discovering the Clockwork Vault
beats.description: The Antechamber establishes the vault’s history, the century-sealed entrance, the failure of the Great Orrery, and the only possible route to freedom. The player is not tested here; the purpose is to establish motivation and make the complete journey understandable before Objective 1 begins.

beats.title: Receiving the Custodian Key
beats.description: A central pedestal holds the Custodian Key. Vex explains that the key is not the exit key; it grants access to the first mechanism that must be restored. The pedestal, sealed entrance, and Objective 1 gate remain readable within the same onboarding route.

beats.title: Opening the First Objective
beats.description: After the briefing, the player takes the Custodian Key and uses it on the Resonance Engine seal. The keyed gate opens and hands control directly into Objective 1.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: When the Custodian Key is accepted by the first seal, the Resonance Engine door opens. Vex gives a concise objective briefing and the story moves from mystery into action.

gameplay_flow.title: The Resonance Engine
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The player enters a puzzle chamber containing three pillars. Each pillar has an upper lever, lower lever, pressure plate, and colored indicator lamp. Twelve books are scattered around the chamber with no required reading order.

beats.title: Read the Partial Door Display
beats.description: The display near the exit reveals only one part of the required combination: the Middle pillar must be Brown. The Left color, Right color, and the one pillar that must pulse remain unknown. The display never reveals any lever combination.

beats.title: Search Scattered Books for Missing Information
beats.description: The twelve books are a mixed set rather than a sequence: two explain machine rules, eight provide useful clues, and two are harmless maintenance/lore decoys. The rule books explain TOP → BOTTOM lever reading and that pressure plates control steady/pulsing behavior rather than color. The useful books gradually narrow the hidden target to Left = Orange, Right = Purple, and Pulse = Left. A player who finds useful books first may solve faster; reading all twelve is not required.

beats.title: Experiment with the Pillars
beats.description: The books do not teach all twelve lever-to-color mappings. The player tries the four TOP → BOTTOM lever combinations on each pillar and reads the immediate lamp feedback to discover how that pillar produces its available colors. The pressure plate independently switches that pillar between steady and pulsing without changing the selected color.

beats.title: Match the Hidden Final State
beats.description: The valid door solution is Left Orange and pulsing, Middle Brown and steady, Right Purple and steady. The player combines the book deductions with lever experimentation until all three live pillar states match this complete target simultaneously.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: When Left = Orange + pulse, Middle = Brown + steady, and Right = Purple + steady are confirmed together, the Resonance Engine restores, the completion boundary is secured, and the Broken Gallery opens.

gameplay_flow.title: The Broken Gallery
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The Broken Gallery is a three-level route-selection challenge. Each level provides three possible routes, checkpoint-local resource barrels, and marked positions where construction blocks or ladders may be placed.

beats.title: Level 1 — Two Viable Routes
beats.description: The player searches the Level 1 barrels, reads the three broken route options, and repairs only marked placement positions. The middle and right routes are viable; the left route requires more material than the available allocation. A viable Level 1 crossing requires 12 blocks. Choosing poorly may consume the available resource before the route can be finished.

beats.title: Level 2 — One Viable Route
beats.description: At the second checkpoint the same loop returns with a harder resource problem. The player receives an authored allocation for a crossing that requires 20 blocks and 3 ladders. Only the right route is viable. Ladders, like blocks, can be placed only at marked authored positions.

beats.title: Local Retry and Resource Recovery
beats.description: If the player exhausts the current level’s resource on an incomplete route or the configured level time expires, the player returns to that level checkpoint. Temporary blocks/ladders placed during the failed attempt are removed, the checkpoint resource search becomes available again, and completed earlier levels remain complete.

beats.title: Level 3 — Gremlin Time Challenge
beats.description: All three Level 3 routes are initially viable. The player chooses one, collects the checkpoint resource, and must reach at least 50% of that route before the authored time threshold. If the threshold is missed, the player returns to Checkpoint 3, the failed route becomes unavailable for that run while an alternative remains, and the player searches for resource again before choosing another active route.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: Objective 2 completes when the player successfully clears Level 3 and reaches the exit into the Warden Halls. The full Gallery does not restart after a checkpoint-local failure.

gameplay_flow.title: The Warden Halls
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The Warden Halls are a three-level trap maze built around wall lasers, floor traps, and swinging ceiling axes. The Echo Pebble is an unlimited tool with a 3-second cooldown between throws.

beats.title: Learn the Three Trap Families
beats.description: Wall lasers communicate a visible beam/sensor state and may be crossed by timing or temporarily disabled. Floor traps are ground hazards that must be avoided. Swinging axes move across the corridor from the ceiling and must be crossed by reading their timing.

beats.title: Use the Echo Pebble on Valid Laser Targets
beats.description: Throwing the Echo Pebble at an authored wall-laser sensor temporarily disables that laser. At selected encounters, the Pebble can instead strike an authored hanging stone so it drops into the beam path and blocks the laser. Floor traps and swinging axes never accept the Pebble as a disable solution.

beats.title: Respect the Cooldown and Hazard Consequences
beats.description: Pebble supply is unlimited, but each throw starts a 3-second cooldown before the next throw. Laser contact deals 10 gameplay damage, Weakness II for 5 seconds, and Slowness I for 3 seconds. Floor-trap contact deals 5 gameplay damage, Slowness II for 5 seconds, and Blindness for 3 seconds. Swinging-axe contact deals 10 gameplay damage, knocks the player backward, applies Weakness II for 5 seconds, and Slowness I for 3 seconds.

beats.title: Checkpoint Recovery
beats.description: Each Warden level has its own checkpoint. If gameplay health reaches zero from trap damage, the player returns to the active level checkpoint in a safe recovered state. Earlier completed Warden levels remain complete.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: After clearing the third trap level, the player reaches the inner gate and enters the Gremlin’s Workshop for the final restoration objective.

gameplay_flow.title: The Gremlin’s Workshop
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The Workshop contains the Power Generator, three Great Orrery rings, and an authored network of power paths controlled by 90-degree L-shaped rotator junctions.

beats.title: Level 1 — Generator to Ring 1
beats.description: The player learns the routing rule by rotating L-junctions until one continuous powered path reaches Ring 1. Each rotator connects exactly two orthogonal directions, so an incorrect orientation visibly interrupts the route.

beats.title: Level 2 — Ring 1 to Ring 2
beats.description: The player extends the same live network from Ring 1 toward Ring 2. Earlier power must remain connected; the puzzle is cumulative rather than three unrelated ring solutions.

beats.title: First Gremlin Sabotage — Route Swap
beats.description: About 20 seconds after Ring 1 and Ring 2 are successfully connected, the Gremlin disrupts the route used to reach Ring 2. The previous route receives an unmistakable blocked state, while a previously blocked alternate route opens. The player must reroute through the newly available path and restore the continuous Generator → Ring 1 → Ring 2 network.

beats.title: Level 3 — Ring 2 to Ring 3 with Rollback Events
beats.description: The player continues toward Ring 3. When validated Ring 2 → Ring 3 route progress reaches 50%, the Gremlin rotates two previously correct rotators on the Generator → Ring 1 connection, forcing the player to return and repair that earlier link. At 80% progress, the Gremlin rotates three previously correct rotators on the Ring 1 → Ring 2 connection, again removing power until the player repairs the earlier network.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: The objective completes only when the Power Generator, Ring 1, Ring 2, and Ring 3 are all continuously connected after the sabotage events. The Great Orrery awakens and the Clockwork exit begins opening.

gameplay_flow.title: The Vault Awakens
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: When all three rings remain powered, the Great Orrery begins turning for the first time in centuries.

beats.title: Awakening the Great Orrery
beats.description: Energy travels backward through every completed chamber: the Resonance Engine synchronizes, gallery guide lights return, Warden systems settle, and the century-sealed entrance begins unlocking. The ending confirms that the player restored one connected machine rather than completing unrelated challenges.

beats.title: Resolving the Custodian’s Story
beats.description: Custodian Vex thanks the player and acknowledges that the vault was waiting for someone capable of restoring it. The player receives the Clockwork Wayfinder reward after the completion record has been saved.

beats.title: Leaving the Clockwork Vault
beats.description: After the result and Clockwork Wayfinder reward state are secured, the player follows the safe return route to the Holding Area while the assigned lane begins cleanup and reset.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: The player exits through the reopened gateway as the Great Orrery continues operating behind them. Temporary gameplay state is cleared and the assigned lane is prepared for reuse.

global_development.title: Development Overview
global_development.subtitle: Project-wide development
global_development.overview: Build one isolated Clockwork journey per active player lane. Shared runtime systems own session start, transitions, pause, data, interruption, and reset, while each objective owns its local mechanic and completion state.

flow.title: Foundation Setup
flow.description: Prepare isolated lanes, holding area, start gate, transitions, shared identifiers, and reset ownership.

flow.title: Shared Systems
flow.description: Implement Vex, game-time, pause, inventory, permissions, feedback, data boundaries, and platform score inputs.

flow.title: Station Integration
flow.description: Connect Introduction, four objectives, ending, and all station-boundary saves in fixed story order.

flow.title: Verification and Reuse
flow.description: Validate parity across lanes, no cross-lane leakage, complete event delivery, and reset under 30 seconds.

items.title: Lane Architecture
details: Use one player per lane and five station cells plus ending space.
Prevent visual, audio, entity, particle, and state leakage between lanes.
Start the session only when the player exits the holding-area gate.
items.result: Defines safe parallel ownership for school sessions.

items.title: Story and Navigation
details: Keep fixed order: Antechamber → Resonance → Gallery → Warden → Workshop → Ending.
Use one-way corridors for briefing, cleanup, boundary save, and next-station activation.
items.result: Maintains one coherent adventure and clean state boundaries.

items.title: Deterministic Treatment
details: Use authored pillar mappings, route viability, route-close behavior, trap cycles/effects, and Gremlin sabotage events.
Do not randomize a gameplay rule or fault effect at runtime unless an authored variant has been separately approved.
items.result: Keeps player conditions readable and verifiable.

items.title: Input and Accessibility
details: Support keyboard, controller, and touch equally.
Use simple interactions, no combat, and no vanilla-knowledge dependency.
Avoid precision parkour. Objective 3 may use gameplay damage and checkpoint recovery as explicitly defined by its hazard rules.
items.result: Preserves the intended accessible puzzle/traversal experience while respecting the approved Warden exception.

items.title: Data and Scoring Boundary
details: Emit raw timestamped events only.
Provide enough evidence for platform-side objective scoring without showing or sending final score from the map.
items.result: Separates gameplay implementation from platform interpretation.

items.title: Reset and Readiness
details: Reset every lane in under 30 seconds.
Test pause, interruption, rejoin, timeout, completion, multi-lane load, checkpoint retry, and no-leakage behavior.
items.result: Makes the map ready for back-to-back use.

notes.title: Lane Isolation
notes.description: Every active player owns one isolated lane; visual, audio, entity, particle, and gameplay state must not leak between lanes.

notes.title: Authored Objective Rules
notes.description: Pillar mapping, Gallery route viability, Warden trap effects, and Workshop sabotage remain reproducible for equivalent sessions.

notes.title: Score Boundary
notes.description: The map emits raw gameplay evidence; Objective Scores are calculated outside the Minecraft experience.

notes.title: Reusable Lane
notes.description: A lane returns to service only after objective, ending, inventory, entity, timing, temporary-block, trap, route, and sabotage states are verified clean.

global_development.title: Game System
global_development.subtitle: Project-wide development
global_development.overview: The shared runtime controls lane ownership, objective order, Custodian Vex, game-time, pause, inventory, permissions, transitions, and interruption handling. Objective mechanics plug into this lifecycle without changing its global rules.

flow.title: Session and Lane Setup
flow.description: Assign one player, initialize lane ownership, and keep the holding area isolated until the start gate.

flow.title: Station Lifecycle
flow.description: Run briefing → active → complete/timeout/interrupted → transition with one authoritative station state.

flow.title: Pause and Persistence
flow.description: Freeze game-time, player input, and scheduled events; save every boundary and interruption.

flow.title: Ending and Release
flow.description: Complete the session, deliver reward/data, return to lobby, and release the lane only after reset verification.

items.title: Holding Area and Start
details: Contain players until they use the start gate.
Start master/session game-time only after lane entry.
Prevent early visibility of active stations.
items.result: Absorbs uneven classroom joins without shortening gameplay.

items.title: Lane Isolation
details: Own players, entities, effects, sounds, particles, scoreboards, timers, and temporary blocks by lane.
Reject cross-lane interaction and clean lane-owned objects at every boundary.
items.result: Prevents another player’s event from spoiling or changing the experience.

items.title: Custodian Vex
details: Use one persistent guide per lane with concise externalized dialogue.
Pair important instructions with readable UI, in-world state, or authored presentation.
Do not reveal hidden route solutions or clue answers before the player solves them.
items.result: Provides instruction, tone, and readable setback reactions without auto-solving.

items.title: Inventory and Permissions
details: Clear and grant station-specific inventory at entry.
Apply scripted break/place/interact permissions only to current station targets and marked Gallery placement positions.
Remove permissions/items at exit, interruption, and reset.
items.result: Prevents map damage and cross-station state leakage.

items.title: Game-Time and Pause
details: Own all timers, cooldowns, and scheduled events in script game-time.
Pause player/camera input, timers, Echo Pebble cooldown, trap cycles, Gallery thresholds, and Workshop sabotage at exact state.
Keep absolute session hard caps according to the approved session rule.
items.result: Makes pause deterministic without real-time drift.

items.title: Setback Feedback
details: Use telegraph → impact → Vex/UI reaction for Gallery retries, Level 3 route closure, trap damage/checkpoint recovery, and Gremlin sabotage.
Ensure visual treatment carries meaning when audio is muted.
items.result: Makes external setbacks readable and memorable.

items.title: Boundary and Transition
details: Save station data, clear temporary state, close the previous route, brief the next station, and activate only after entry is safe.
Complete, timeout, and interruption must use distinct exit reasons.
items.result: Creates reliable station boundaries.

items.title: Rejoin Behavior
details: Save partial data immediately on disconnect.
Mark station interrupted and restart that station from a clean valid state on rejoin while preserving earlier completed objective results.
items.result: Protects data without resuming into invalid temporary geometry or hazard state.

notes.title: Script-Owned Timing
notes.description: Use Script API / scoreboard-owned timing rather than redstone clocks for objective lifecycle and scheduled events.

notes.title: No Hidden Runtime Rule Changes
notes.description: Gremlin events change visible route availability or rotator orientation; they do not secretly change the learned connection grammar.

notes.title: Localization Ready
notes.description: Keep in-game strings externalized so localized copy can be added without changing gameplay logic.

notes.title: Concurrent Lane Test
notes.description: Shared systems must remain isolated and stable with all supported lanes active together.

global_development.title: Data and Reset
global_development.subtitle: Project-wide development
global_development.overview: Each objective records the raw gameplay events needed to reconstruct its result. Data is saved at objective boundaries and interruptions; the assigned lane is released only after temporary state is cleared, authored structures are restored, and readiness checks pass.

flow.title: Capture
flow.description: Record session, station, action, state, pause, completion, timeout, retry, and interruption events.

flow.title: Persist and Send
flow.description: Buffer safely, save at boundaries, and retry delivery without duplicate semantic events.

flow.title: Clear Runtime State
flow.description: Remove inventory, permissions, entities, particles, scheduled tasks, temporary blocks, effects, and lane properties.

flow.title: Restore and Verify
flow.description: Reload structures, restore defaults, run readiness checks, then release the lane.

items.title: Common Envelope
details: Every event carries anonymous session ID, map ID, station ID, lane ID, build version, event name, and game-time timestamp.
Do not send player name, gamertag, device identifier, platform interpretation, or final map-side score.
items.result: Provides consistent anonymous event ownership.

items.title: Objective Payloads
details: Record Resonance clue/pillar/target states, Gallery resource/route/checkpoint states, Warden Pebble/trap/damage/recovery states, and Workshop rotator/connectivity/sabotage states.
Record pause, completion, timeout, retry, and interruption fields where required.
items.result: Provides platform scoring evidence without aggregation in-world.

items.title: Boundary Save
details: Save and send at station exit, disconnect, ending, and session end.
Use idempotent event IDs or sequence numbers to prevent duplicate delivery after retry.
items.result: Prevents loss and duplication.

items.title: Timing Rules
details: Use game-time timestamps; pause freezes gameplay timing.
Record authored event state exactly, including Gallery route closure, trap contact/effects, Pebble cooldown/disable windows, Workshop route swap, and 50%/80% rotator sabotage.
items.result: Allows fair timing and treatment verification.

items.title: Script Cleanup
details: Cancel scheduled callbacks; clear station state, UI, effects, entities, items, permissions, scoreboards, and lane dynamic properties.
Remove player-placed Gallery blocks/ladders before structure restore.
items.result: Prevents stale runtime logic.

items.title: Structure Restore and Verification
details: Restore all station cells and ending states from approved structures.
Verify doors, targets, clue/pillar states, barrels/resources, route availability, trap cycles, health/effects, rotators, sabotage flags, items, guide, and timers.
Release lane only after all readiness checks pass within 30 seconds.
items.result: Guarantees pristine reuse.

items.title: Interrupted Sessions
details: Preserve partial data and mark incomplete.
On rejoin, restart the interrupted station from an authored clean state and retain earlier completed objective results.
items.result: Protects evidence while avoiding corrupted temporary state.

items.title: Delivery or Reset Failure
details: Queue failed data sends for retry and keep semantic IDs stable.
Keep a lane unavailable when reset verification fails and surface a technical error for staff.
items.result: Prevents silent data loss and unsafe reuse.

notes.title: Objective-Owned Payloads
notes.description: Each objective emits only the raw fields needed to reconstruct its gameplay result and authored treatment state.

notes.title: Raw Data Stays Raw
notes.description: Platform scoring or interpretation never changes the event payload produced by the map.

notes.title: Reset Is Runtime-Critical
notes.description: A lane is not reusable until cleanup and structure restoration complete within the approved reset target.

notes.title: No State Carryover
notes.description: Clue/target states, route closures, trap effects, cooldowns, sabotage states, inventory, temporary blocks, and objective flags must not survive reset.

global_development.title: Gameplay Development
global_development.subtitle: Project-wide development
global_development.overview: Every playable area follows the same lifecycle: prepare a clean area, activate its mechanic after safe entry, validate completion and save the result, then clear temporary state before handing the player to the next objective.

flow.title: Prepare Area
flow.description: Restore the objective area, set lane ownership, grant required inventory/permissions, and present the next clear player goal.

flow.title: Run Mechanic
flow.description: Activate only the current objective, own its game-time, feedback, setback/recovery behavior, and lane-local state.

flow.title: Complete and Save
flow.description: Validate the objective end condition once, record the required raw result evidence, and freeze the completed state for transition.

flow.title: Transition and Restore
flow.description: Move the player through the safe handoff, remove temporary state, and restore the previous objective for reuse.

items.title: Activation and Ownership
details: Activate a mechanic only after the assigned player reaches its safe entry state.
Keep timers, entities, effects, inventory, permissions, health/recovery logic, and temporary objects owned by the active lane/objective.
Do not activate the next objective until the current handoff is complete.
items.result: Only one objective controls the player at a time.

items.title: Completion and Handoff
details: Validate the approved end condition once.
Freeze or close the completed mechanic before transition.
Save the objective result at the boundary, then open the next safe route.
items.result: Progression cannot duplicate, skip, or overlap objective states.

items.title: Goal and Feedback
details: Present one clear immediate goal when an objective becomes active.
Pair important interactions or setbacks with visible feedback; audio may reinforce but not replace meaning.
Use Custodian Vex for concise instruction and transition framing.
items.result: Players can understand what changed and what to do next.

items.title: Boundary Save
details: Record raw gameplay evidence required by the current objective.
Pause script-owned timing during pause.
On interruption, keep completed objective results and restart the interrupted objective from a clean state.
items.result: Partial sessions remain recoverable without corrupting previous progress.

items.title: Objective Cleanup
details: Clear temporary inventory, permissions, callbacks, effects, entities, player-placed blocks, health/recovery state, and objective-local flags.
Restore authored structures and initial mechanic state.
Release the lane only after readiness verification succeeds.
items.result: Every objective can be replayed from the same authored starting state.

notes.title: Single Active Objective
notes.description: Only the current objective may own active gameplay input, timers, and temporary state.

notes.title: Boundary Save
notes.description: Completion and interruption both create explicit boundary records before state changes.

notes.title: Platform Scoring
notes.description: Minecraft records raw evidence; Objective Scores remain platform-side.

notes.title: Journey Verification
notes.description: The complete journey must pass end-to-end and concurrent-lane testing before handoff.

gameplay.context: The player enters the protected Antechamber and meets Custodian Vex. A central pedestal holds the Custodian Key, and the Resonance Engine seal is the visible next destination.
gameplay.main_objective: Listen to Vex’s briefing, collect the Custodian Key, and use it on the Resonance Engine seal.
gameplay.result: The seal opens and the Resonance Engine becomes accessible. The Antechamber creates no Objective Score.
gameplay.purpose: Establish story, navigation, pickup/use interaction, and the next destination without adding a separate warm-up minigame.
gameplay.start_condition: The player leaves the holding area in Adventure mode with the assigned lane active and the Antechamber reset.
gameplay.end_condition: The Custodian Key is accepted by the Resonance Engine seal and the objective door opens.
gameplay.blocked_or_fail_condition: There is no lethal or permanent fail state. If the key interaction is missed or interrupted, Vex repeats the cue and the key/seal state remains recoverable.
gameplay.scoring_criteria: No Objective Score. Completion is recorded as story progression only.

packages.title: The Resonance Engine

gameplay.context: The Resonance Engine chamber contains three puzzle pillars with upper/lower levers, pressure plates, and colored indicator lamps. Twelve books are scattered through the chamber with no required reading order, while the door display reveals only Middle = Brown.
gameplay.main_objective: Use the scattered books to discover the missing Left and Right target colors and which pillar must pulse, then experiment with each pillar’s lever combinations until the machine reaches the complete hidden door solution.
gameplay.result: Left is Orange and pulsing, Middle is Brown and steady, and Right is Purple and steady; the Resonance Engine restores and the Broken Gallery route opens.
gameplay.purpose: Create a light deduction-and-experimentation puzzle where books reveal the missing target information and direct machine testing reveals how each lever pair produces color.
gameplay.start_condition: All three pillars are reset, twelve books are scattered and readable, all pressure plates begin in their authored initial state, and the door display shows only Middle = Brown with the other target information unknown.
gameplay.end_condition: Left = Orange + pulse, Middle = Brown + steady, and Right = Purple + steady are simultaneously active.
gameplay.blocked_or_fail_condition: There is no permanent fail state. Lever and pressure-plate states remain reversible; at the station deadline, partial book/pillar progress is recorded and the journey follows the session timeout rule.
gameplay.scoring_criteria: Objective Score 0–100 based on Pillar Completion, Clue Coverage, and Rule Application.

packages.title: The Broken Gallery

gameplay.context: The player enters a ruined crossing divided into three checkpoint levels. Each level presents three route choices, checkpoint-local resource barrels, and marked positions where blocks or ladders may be placed.
gameplay.main_objective: Clear Level 1, Level 2, and the Level 3 Gremlin time challenge by choosing a viable route, using only the available resource, and reaching each next checkpoint.
gameplay.result: The player clears the third route level and reaches the Warden Halls entrance.
gameplay.purpose: Create a route-reading and limited-resource traversal challenge where incorrect choices produce a local reset instead of permanent failure.
gameplay.start_condition: Level 1 is reset, its resource barrels are available, all temporary placement positions are empty, and the three route choices are readable.
gameplay.end_condition: The player successfully reaches the exit beyond Level 3.
gameplay.blocked_or_fail_condition: Resource exhaustion or configured level-time expiry resets only the active level. In Level 3, missing the 50% progress threshold additionally closes the failed route while another alternative remains. Earlier completed levels stay complete.
gameplay.scoring_criteria: Objective Score 0–100 based on Objective Progress, Resource Planning, Timed-Route Adaptation, and Recovery Independence.

player_flow.title: Level 1 — Choose Between Two Viable Routes
player_flow.description: Search the checkpoint barrels, inspect three routes, and use 12 blocks on a viable middle/right crossing without wasting the allocation on the non-viable left route.

player_flow.title: Reset and Relearn When Needed
player_flow.description: If the attempt exhausts its resource or level time, return to the current checkpoint, remove temporary placements, resupply, and try another route.

player_flow.title: Level 2 — Find the Single Viable Route
player_flow.description: Use the authored 20-block + 3-ladder allocation; only the right route can be completed and all placements remain restricted to marked positions.

player_flow.title: Level 3 — Beat the Gremlin Threshold
player_flow.description: Choose any initially viable route and reach at least 50% progress before the configured threshold. A failed route closes and the player returns to Checkpoint 3 to resupply and choose another active route.

player_flow.title: Reach the Warden Halls
player_flow.description: Clear the final route, save checkpoint/resource/retry evidence, and open the next chamber.

level_design.overview: Build the Gallery as three readable route-selection levels. Every level exposes three choices while keeping the viable answer hidden from the player. Barrels, placement markers, reset geometry, and checkpoints must be readable as one repeatable local loop.

flow.title: Level 1 — Basic Route Reading
flow.description: Present three routes with middle/right viable and left deliberately over-budget.

flow.title: Level 3 — Timed Route Commitment
flow.description: Make all three routes initially viable, then visibly close a failed route after the 50% progress deadline is missed.

flow.description: Frame the Warden Halls entrance as the clear destination after Level 3 success.

packages.title: The Warden Halls

gameplay.context: The Warden Halls are a three-level trap maze using wall lasers, floor traps, and swinging ceiling axes. Echo Pebble is unlimited but has a 3-second throw cooldown and only interacts with authored laser solutions.
gameplay.main_objective: Reach the inner gate by disabling or blocking selected wall lasers, avoiding floor traps, timing swinging axes, and recovering from trap damage at level checkpoints.
gameplay.result: The player clears all three Warden levels and the Gremlin’s Workshop route opens.
gameplay.purpose: Create a readable hazard-navigation challenge where the player distinguishes Pebble-valid laser solutions from traps that must be avoided or timed.

items.title: Unlimited Tool / Cooldown
details: Keep Echo Pebble supply unlimited for the active objective.
After every valid or invalid throw that consumes the throw action, block the next throw for 3 seconds of game-time and expose a readable recharge/ready state.
Freeze/resume the cooldown with shared pause behavior.
items.result: Prevents spam while keeping the puzzle independent of ammunition count.

items.title: Valid Targets
details: Accept authored wall-laser sensors and authored hanging-stone targets only.
On a sensor hit, disable that laser for 4 seconds of game-time before its authored cycle resumes.
On a hanging-stone hit, move the authored stone into its beam-blocking state for that encounter until local reset/completion.
Reject floor traps and swinging axes as disable targets.
items.result: Preserves the approved difference between laser solutions and avoidance/timing hazards.

items.title: Wall Laser Contact
details: Apply 10 gameplay damage per valid contact tick/event according to the authored beam collision guard.
Apply Weakness II for 5 seconds and Slowness I for 3 seconds.
Prevent duplicate damage from one collision frame beyond the intended contact cadence.
items.result: Makes forcing through an active laser costly and slows immediate follow-up movement.

items.title: Floor Trap Contact
details: Apply 5 gameplay damage.
Apply Slowness II for 5 seconds and Blindness for 3 seconds.
Debounce one trap activation so standing on one trigger does not create unintended duplicate stacks.
items.result: Punishes careless footing without changing objective progress.

items.title: Swinging Axe Contact
details: Apply 10 gameplay damage and authored backward knockback.
Apply Weakness II for 5 seconds and Slowness I for 3 seconds.
Tie damage to the authored active swing/contact window.
items.result: Makes incorrect timing visibly costly and pushes the player away from the hazard.

items.title: Gameplay-Health Recovery
details: If gameplay health reaches zero, clear invalid lingering hit states, restore the player to a safe gameplay-health/effect state, and return them to the active Warden level checkpoint.
Preserve earlier completed Warden levels and reset only encounter-local states that must be replayable from the checkpoint.
items.result: Converts hazard defeat into local time loss rather than full-objective restart.

items.title: Objective Completion

items.result: Creates a clear station boundary with meaningful partial evidence.

packages.title: The Gremlin’s Workshop

gameplay.context: The Workshop contains the Power Generator, three Great Orrery rings, and an authored power-routing field of 90-degree L rotators.
gameplay.main_objective: Keep one continuous network from Generator → Ring 1 → Ring 2 → Ring 3 while repairing the route swap and two later Gremlin rotator-sabotage events.
gameplay.result: Generator and all three rings are continuously powered, the Great Orrery restores, and the Clockwork exit opens.
gameplay.purpose: Test power-routing understanding, memory of previously solved sections, and adaptation when an external Gremlin visibly changes the network.
gameplay.start_condition: The authored routing field is reset, Power Generator and Ring 1–3 are readable, normal blockers are in their initial states, and no Gremlin event has fired.
gameplay.end_condition: Power Generator, Ring 1, Ring 2, and Ring 3 are all continuously connected after the 20-second route swap and 50%/80% rollback events.
gameplay.blocked_or_fail_condition: There is no permanent fail state. Rotators remain reversible and the authored blocker changes always leave a valid route; progress may be interrupted until earlier damaged connections are repaired.
gameplay.scoring_criteria: Objective Score 0–100 based on Ring Completion, Gremlin Adaptation, and Independent Progress.

player_flow.description: Complete only when Generator and all three rings are simultaneously connected, save the full action/sabotage sequence, lock puzzle input, and begin the ending.

items.title: Rotator Solver

items.title: Post-Ring-2 Sabotage
details: About 20 seconds after Ring 1 and Ring 2 are connected, run the Gremlin route-swap event once using game-time.

items.title: 50% Progress Sabotage

On first reach of 50%, rotate exactly two authored previously correct rotators on the Generator → Ring 1 route to their sabotage orientations.
Recalculate power and require the player to restore the damaged earlier link before final completion can remain valid.
items.result: Tests awareness of the whole network, not only the newest route segment.

items.title: 80% Progress Sabotage
details: On first reach of 80%, rotate exactly three authored previously correct rotators on the Ring 1 → Ring 2 route to their sabotage orientations.
Recalculate power and require the player to repair that earlier connection before Ring 3 completion can resolve.
Each rollback event fires once per session and remains idempotent across pause/resume.
items.result: Creates the final Gremlin interruption before full restoration.

items.title: Full Network Completion

Lock puzzle interaction only after the valid completion record is committed, then begin the Great Orrery restoration presentation.
At timeout preserve rotator orientations, blocker states, ring connectivity, route progress, sabotage-fired flags, and action history.
items.result: Defines the final objective boundary without bypassing a broken earlier link.

completion_data.interrupted_completion_behavior: If disconnected after Workshop completion, preserve the completed objective state and finish reward/session delivery safely on rejoin or platform retry; do not replay or double-grant the ending.
completion_data.duplicate_prevention: Ending start, session completion, final send, Clockwork Wayfinder grant, and lane release are idempotent per session.
completion_data.final_result_relationship: Closes the session containing the four Objective Scores; no Ending Objective Score is added.
completion_data.player_facing_display: Show the restoration payoff, Vex recognition, reward, and return cues; do not expose platform scoring/analysis.
completion_data.telemetry_export: Export ending callbacks, session completion, reward/save/retry state, return, and reset verification; no new objective score.

reset: Clear temporary inventory/effects/permissions and restore every objective cell plus ending-specific doors, Vex/Gremlin/Orrery presentation state, lights/audio/particles, reward markers, and return-route state.
Keep the lane unavailable until reset verification confirms every station is back at its authored starting condition.
developer.reset_result: The completed player is safely returned and the assigned Clockwork lane is verified reusable-ready.

terms.label: Session result
terms.definition: The stored completion record containing raw completion and reward state, not a player-facing score.

terms.label: Pending Recovery Record
terms.definition: The fallback record created when primary session storage cannot complete.

terms.label: Idempotent reward
terms.definition: A reward operation that cannot grant the same cosmetic reward twice.

terms.label: Lane verification
terms.definition: The checks confirming that the completed lane is clean before reuse.

acceptance: Vault Restored reaches its defined end condition without creating an unrecoverable player state.
Vault Restored preserves the approved player-facing behavior, data/result boundary, and lane isolation rules.
Vault Restored reset restores the authored starting state before the assigned lane is reused.
